answer:
Given a simply supported beam of length $L = 10\text{ m}$ with:
- Point load of $50\text{ kN}$ at $C$ ($2\text{ m}$ from $A$)
- UDL of $10\text{ kN/m}$ over a length of $4\text{ m}$ starting $6\text{ m}$ from $A$
- Point load of $40\text{ kN}$ at $D$ ($6\text{ m}$ from $A$, right at the start of the UDL)

**1. Support Reactions ($R_A$ and $R_B$):**
Taking moments about $A$ ($\sum M_A = 0$):
$R_B \times 10 - 50 \times 2 - (40 \times 6) - (10 \times 4 \times (6 + \frac{4}{2})) = 0$
$10 R_B = 100 + 240 + (40 \times 8) = 340 + 320 = 660$
$R_B = 66\text{ kN}$

Using $\sum F_y = 0$:
$R_A + R_B = 50 + 40 + (10 \times 4) = 130\text{ kN}$
$R_A = 130 - 66 = 64\text{ kN}$

**2. Shear Force (S.F.) Calculations:**
- Just right of $A$ ($x = 0$): $SF = +64\text{ kN}$
- Just left of $C$ ($x = 2^-$): $SF = +64\text{ kN}$
- Just right of $C$ ($x = 2^+$): $SF = 64 - 50 = +14\text{ kN}$
- At $D$ ($x = 6^-$): $SF = +14\text{ kN}$
- Just right of $D$ ($x = 6^+$): $SF = 14 - 40 = -26\text{ kN}$
- At $B$ ($x = 10^-$): $SF = -26 - (10 \times 4) = -66\text{ kN}$

**3. Bending Moment (B.M.) Calculations:**
- At $A$ ($x = 0$): $BM = 0$
- At $C$ ($x = 2\text{ m}$): $BM = 64 \times 2 = 128\text{ kNm}$
- At $D$ ($x = 6\text{ m}$): $BM = (64 \times 6) - (50 \times (6-2)) = 384 - 200 = 184\text{ kNm}$
- At $B$ ($x = 10\text{ m}$): $BM = 0$
proTip: Always break down UDL into a single equivalent point load acting at its centroid when calculating support reactions.
